scenarios.title: A Rift at Home
text: {DAD} has stopped answering {J}'s calls. {MUM} answers, but only to say 'he's sleeping' at 7pm. {SIB} finally tells him the truth: 'They think you've forgotten us.'
The family group chat has gone silent for three weeks. When {J} posts a photo from training, nobody reacts. Not even {MUM}.

choices.label: Go home, now
choices.hint: Costs fitness and a day. Saves everything else.
choices.text: He turns up unannounced. {DAD} opens the door, looks at him for a long time, and steps aside to let him in. They talk until 3am. Some of it is shouting. Most of it isn't.

choices.label: A long, honest phone call
choices.text: He apologises for every missed call. {MUM} cries. {DAD} listens without speaking, then says: 'Come home soon.'

choices.label: Send money to fix it
choices.text: He sends a large transfer. {DAD} sends it back with a message: 'We don't want your money. We want our son.'

scenarios.title: {SIB} Is Angry
text: {SIB} posts something online: 'Funny how some people only remember their family when they need a photo.' Everyone knows who it's about.
{SIB} calls, furious: {MUM} has been ill for two weeks and nobody told {J} because 'you're always too busy'.

choices.label: Call {SIB} and listen
choices.text: He just listens. Forty minutes of anger, then tears, then 'I just miss you, idiot.' They make a plan for the next holiday.

choices.label: Defend yourself
choices.desc: 'You don't know how hard this is.'
choices.text: It turns into a fight. Both of them say things they'll regret. {MUM} has to mediate from a sickbed.

scenarios.title: The Group Chat Without You
text: {J} finds out by accident: there's a new group chat. Everyone from the old crew is in it. He isn't. It's called 'the real ones'.
{BFf} posts photos from a weekend away with all their old friends. {J} wasn't invited. He hadn't replied to a message in a month, so maybe that's fair.
scenarios.prompt: Your friends have moved on without you.

choices.label: Call {BFf} and be honest
choices.desc: 'I miss you. I've been a bad friend.'
choices.text: {BFf} is quiet, then: 'We thought you'd outgrown us.' 'Never,' says {J}. The next week, he's back in the original chat. The new one is quietly deleted.

choices.label: Organise a reunion, your treat
choices.hint: Grand gesture. Could feel like buying friendship.

out.text: Everyone comes. It's awkward for an hour, then it's like nothing ever changed.
Half of them come. One says, quietly, 'You can't just pay to fix this.' He's right.

choices.label: Accept it
choices.text: He accepts it. His world gets a little smaller and a little quieter.

scenarios.title: The Dressing Room Turns
text: {CAP} closes the dressing-room door after training. 'We need to talk about you.' Eight players are sitting down. Nobody is smiling.
Someone has moved {J}'s locker to the corner by the showers. It's a message. Everyone saw who moved it. Nobody says anything.
scenarios.prompt: The squad has a problem with you.

choices.label: Listen to every complaint
choices.text: He sits and listens for twenty minutes. Some of it is unfair. Most of it isn't. At the end he says, 'You're right. I'll fix it.' {CAP} nods once.

choices.label: Fight back
choices.desc: 'You've all got a problem with success.'
choices.text: It escalates fast. A shove. Coaches run in. {Mf} has to choose between {J} and his senior players. He doesn't choose {J}.

choices.label: Buy everyone dinner, apologise there
choices.text: A long table, a lot of food, one short speech. It doesn't fix everything. It fixes enough.

scenarios.title: One of the Leaders
text: Without anyone announcing it, {J} has become one of the voices of the dressing room. Young players ask his advice. Senior players ask his opinion. {Mf} asks him to speak at half-time.
{CAP} tells {J}: 'When I'm gone, this is your dressing room.' It isn't a joke.
scenarios.prompt: What kind of leader are you?

choices.label: Lead by example
choices.text: He says little and works harder than anyone. The young players copy everything he does, including the way he ties his boots.

choices.label: Be the voice
choices.text: He starts holding teammates to account out loud. The standards rise. A couple of players resent it. Results improve.

choices.label: Look after the young ones
choices.text: He takes the academy kids under his wing: lifts, advice, phone calls home. One day they'll tell interviewers about him.

scenarios.title: The Board Has Had Enough
text: A letter from the club's legal department: a formal warning about 'conduct and commitment'. Nobody explains what that means. Everybody knows what it means.
President {PRESl} walks past {J} in the corridor and doesn't say hello. Then a director tells his agent that 'offers would be considered'.
scenarios.prompt: The club hierarchy is turning against you.

ok.text: An hour in the president's office. Firm handshakes, frank words. {PRESl} says, 'I like a player who looks me in the eye.' The warning is withdrawn.

bad.text: {PRESl} keeps him waiting forty minutes and gives him ten. Nothing changes except {J}'s blood pressure.

choices.label: Do everything the club asks
choices.text: Every event, every handshake, every photo. It takes weeks. Slowly, the corridor greetings return.

choices.label: Hand in a transfer request
choices.desc: If they don't want you, leave.
choices.text: The request is accepted with indecent speed. He's on the transfer list by Friday.

scenarios.title: The Grey Weeks
text: Everything has gone grey. Football, food, music, messages. {J} goes to training, comes home, sits in the dark. He hasn't told anyone. The club psychologist has noticed anyway.
{J} cancels plans with everyone. He doesn't want to talk. He scrolls, sleeps badly, trains on autopilot. Somewhere along the way, he stopped enjoying football.
scenarios.prompt: Something is wrong, and it isn't your body.

choices.label: Talk to the club psychologist
choices.hint: The bravest thing you'll do this year.
choices.text: The first session he barely speaks. The second, he can't stop. It isn't fixed. But it's started.

choices.label: Tell someone you love
choices.text: He calls and just says, 'I'm not okay.' The person on the other end doesn't panic. They just stay on the phone. That's everything.

choices.label: Push through alone
choices.text: He tells himself it's nothing. It isn't nothing. It shows on the pitch, in the dressing room, at home.

scenarios.title: Burnout
text: {J}'s hands are shaking before training. His heart races at night. The sports scientist shows him the data — heart-rate variability, sleep, reaction times — and says one word: 'burnout'.
In the middle of a routine drill, {J} stops, sits down on the grass and can't explain why. The physio sits next to him. Nobody rushes him.
scenarios.prompt: Your body and mind are at breaking point.

choices.label: Take a full week off
choices.hint: You'll miss a match. You'll save your season.
choices.text: A week at home with the phone off. {MUM}'s cooking, long walks, sleep. He comes back a different person.

choices.label: Cut everything except football
choices.desc: No media, no events, no extras.
choices.hint: Some people won't like being cut.
choices.text: He cancels every sponsor event and interview for a month. The board grumbles. His body thanks him.

choices.label: Push through
choices.text: He keeps going. Something has to give, and in football, something always does.

scenarios.title: Bringing It Home
text: {J} snapped at {Pf} over nothing — the wrong brand of rice. She stares at him. 'This isn't about rice, is it?'
{Pf} finds {J} awake at 4am, sitting in the kitchen. 'Talk to me,' she says. He doesn't know where to start.
scenarios.prompt: The pressure is leaking into your relationship.

choices.label: Tell her everything
choices.text: He talks until sunrise. She doesn't try to fix anything. She just listens. He sleeps for four hours, the best four hours in weeks.

choices.label: 'I'm fine.'
choices.text: 'I'm fine.' She goes back to bed. He stays in the kitchen. Both of them are awake until morning, in different rooms.

scenarios.title: A Good Balance
text: For once, everything is in balance: family calls on Sundays, friends on Fridays, training every day, sleep every night. {J} has found a rhythm.
{J} realises he hasn't felt anxious in weeks. His family is close, his friends are close, and football feels like a game again.

choices.label: Write down what's working
choices.desc: Remember this for the hard days.
choices.text: He writes it all down: the routines, the people, the small things. On hard days months from now, he'll read it again.

choices.label: Push for more on the pitch
choices.desc: Use the stability to level up.
choices.text: With his life settled, he trains with a new hunger. The coaches notice the difference.

scenarios.title: A Friend Talks to the Papers
text: {OUT} has a story about {J}'s 'loneliness' and 'arrogance', based on 'friends from home who feel abandoned'. One quote sounds exactly like {BFf}.
A podcast plays an anonymous voice note: an old friend saying {J} 'changed when the money came'.
scenarios.prompt: Neglect at home has become a media story.

choices.label: Call {BFf} first, the papers never
choices.desc: Fix the friendship, ignore the story.
choices.text: {BFf} admits he was angry and said too much to the wrong person. They argue, then they don't. The story dies; the friendship doesn't.

choices.label: Issue a statement
choices.text: His statement is fair and firm. It keeps the story alive another day. The friendship gets colder.

scenarios.title: {MUM} on Television
text: A national TV show visits {J}'s family home. {MUM} has prepared food for forty people. {DAD} has prepared one sentence and repeats it every time a camera points at him.
{MUM} has been invited onto a morning show to talk about raising a footballer. She's terrified. She's also bought a new dress.

choices.label: Video-call in live, surprise her
choices.text: His face appears on the studio screen. {MUM} screams on live television. The clip is the most-watched moment of the show's year.

choices.label: Let her shine on her own
choices.text: She's wonderful: funny, warm, slightly embarrassing. {J} watches it six times.

scenarios.title: The Fans Blame {Pf}
text: With {J} playing badly, some fans have found a scapegoat: {Pf}. Her comments are full of abuse. Someone has written her name on a banner.
A fan forum thread titled 'Is {J}'s girlfriend ruining his career?' has two hundred replies. {Pf} has read all of them.
scenarios.prompt: The fans are attacking your partner.

choices.label: Defend her loudly
choices.hint: She'll feel protected. Fans may turn further.
choices.text: 'Criticise me. Never her.' Most fans respect it. A few double down. {Pf} saves the post on her phone.

choices.label: Play better
choices.text: He says nothing publicly and trains like a man possessed. {Pf} wishes he'd said something.

choices.label: Protect her privately
choices.text: He hires someone to filter her messages and books her a weekend away. She feels cared for, if not defended.

scenarios.title: The President's Invitation
text: President {PRESl} invites {J} and {Pf} to his box for a big match. The president's wife has asked specifically to meet {Pf}.
The board wants {J} and {Pf} at the club's gala dinner. Front table. Next to the sponsors.

choices.label: Go and charm the room
choices.text: {Pf} charms everyone, including the president's wife, who now calls her weekly. {J}'s position at the club has never been safer.

choices.label: Go alone
choices.desc: Keep her out of club politics.
choices.text: He goes alone. {PRESl} asks where she is. {J} makes an excuse.

scenarios.title: Squad Family Day
text: The club's family day. Squad, partners, kids, parents. {MUM} and {DAD} have been invited and are standing nervously by the buffet.
The squad is hosting a family barbecue. {T} has volunteered {J} to run the grill. He has never run a grill.

choices.label: Introduce your parents to everyone
choices.text: {DAD} ends up deep in conversation with {CAPl} about fishing. {MUM} feeds the entire squad. Two worlds become one.

choices.label: Run the grill
choices.text: He burns everything. The squad eats it anyway, chanting his name. {MUM} quietly takes over.

scenarios.title: A Sponsor Walks Away
text: A letter from {J}'s boot sponsor: they are 'pausing the partnership pending a review of brand values'. In other words: goodbye.
A brand he's worked with for years removes his face from their website overnight. His agent finds out from a fan.
scenarios.prompt: Your image is costing you money.

choices.label: Fix the image first
choices.text: No statements, just steady good behaviour and charity work. In six months, brands start calling again.

choices.label: Hit back at the sponsor
choices.text: His post calling the brand 'fake' goes viral. Every other brand takes note.
